verification.note: Fresh actual coauthor institutional UBC Geography posting of the original Wiley article, https://geog.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/sites/26/2023/03/Cole-obit-published-2023.pdf. Selected 1–3 and 4–6 read, including formation, theoretical turn, collective Atlas and later qualifications;3 visually checked. Received and accepted December 2022, copyright and publication 2023; advance PDF pagination 1–6 retained. The title names Harris as subject, while the author byline on 5 is Wynn and Barnes. Atlas dedication and Habermas engagement are the coauthors’ scholarly testimony, not fresh original Atlas,1991 or 2008 article reading. Critical limits in their account of Reluctant Land, collective credits and missing teacher/student endpoints remain explicit.

sources.scope_note: Named retrospective scholarly readers, with explicit mediated and selected reading limits.

pe139_harris_social_power_1997.note: Fresh actual original BC Studies 38-leaf PDF via successful web-tool text; selected opening 45–48, power discussion 56–60 and concluding 79–82 read with associated notes. Windows include actual 59/n 39 naming Said’s Orientalism,58/n 37 Foucault, and agency and cultural-measurement qualifications 80–82. Direct network retrieval failed; successful original PDF rendering retained privately, no complete body claim. Other spans appearing around retrieved windows were not a full article reading. Fisher praise and criticism remain; no original Said, Fisher, ethnographic or archival witness newly read.

pe139_harris_macdonald_1990.note: Fresh complete original Manitoba History 1990 review read from actual historical-society HTML. Innis paragraph and following quotation are explicitly Harris’s Atlas preface as mediated by MacDonald, not fresh original Atlas reading. Collective authorship, cartographer/designer credit and the reviewer’s concern about conservative synthesis, contested prehistory and possible future alternative schematics remain. Web revision date 11 April 2010 is distinct from original Autumn 1990 publication.

screq_harris_2020.note: Fresh actual licensed UBC Press 35-leaf preview retrieved. Selected introduction 3,9–18, especially own retrospective formation 11–13, read;12 visually checked. Andrew H. Clark’s specific research direction, Hamelin’s archive access and Dechêne’s close Atlas collaboration are stronger missing-endpoint leads. Ouellet’s personal help is acknowledged but the passage does not establish a detailed separate theoretical mechanism. Geographic bounds, Indigenous agency and the collection’s abridgment, renumbered notes and occasional textual changes 18 remain. Remaining selections and postscript unread; this is not a complete book or original article reading.
